roles.title: Quantitative Technologist
roles.eligibility: Posted on the 'Radix Experienced' board (for candidates with prior work experience). No graduation-year gate in the posting text; the application form asks for graduation year/expected completion date and years of post-degree work experience. No stated minimum years.
roles.requirements: Low-level languages: C++ or C, understanding nuances of the language / modern C++ | Data structures, algorithmic complexity, numerical algorithms | Systems architecture: distributed systems and communication | Software architecture: experience in a large codebase | Development process: delivering and deploying software in production | Soft criteria stated verbatim: 'Persistent Drive to Improve', 'Creative Problem Solving and Probabilistic Thinking', 'Team Mindset', 'Mental Flexibility & Self Awareness', 'Orientation for Making Money'
roles.notes: Best single fit on the experienced board for the candidate. Posting states only 'Competitive salary, plus quarterly bonus based on individual performance' - no figure given, so comp left empty. Application asks 'Do you require employer-sponsored work authorization?'; as an EU citizen the answer is no for Amsterdam. Req is multi-city (Chicago / New York / Amsterdam) on a single listing - confirm Amsterdam headcount with the recruiter, since the seat may be allocated to a US office. Radix has ~125 people total across Chicago, NY and Amsterdam, so the Amsterdam team is small.

roles.title: Quantitative Researcher
roles.eligibility: Experienced board. No explicit minimum-experience or graduation-year gate in the posting body; the form collects graduation year and years of post-degree work experience. Unofficial undergraduate transcript required, graduate transcript optional.
roles.requirements: Strong data analysis and intuition | 'Hacking' ability to identify empirical relationships in data | Classical and advanced statistical methods | Understanding of financial products and market microstructure | Programming: 'low-level computer languages like C++, or Python, Java, etc.'
roles.notes: Radix explicitly recruits scientists (applied maths, physics, EE, CS) rather than finance backgrounds, so the candidate's ICLR/AAAI submissions and ISCA workshop paper are directly relevant. Posting says 'Competitive salary, plus quarterly bonus based on individual performance and contribution towards success of others and the firm' - no number stated. Transcript upload is mandatory; have the EPFL unofficial undergrad transcript ready. Multi-city req - confirm the Amsterdam seat exists.

roles.title: Quantitative Technologist (Full-Time - C++ Developer)
roles.eligibility: Posted on the 'Radix University' board, which the firm's site describes as being for 'degree candidates, postdocs, and faculty members'. The posting body states no explicit graduation-year cutoff, but the application form requires expected graduation date and GPA. This is a new-grad channel - a poor fit for someone ~18 months into a job; use the experienced board req instead.
roles.requirements: Low-level languages C or C++; awareness of strength in a particular language | Data structures, algorithmic complexities, numerical algorithms | Systems architecture: distributed systems and communication | Software architecture: large codebase experience | Development processes: delivering and deploying software in production environments
roles.notes: Listed for completeness only. Same substantive job description as the experienced Quantitative Technologist req; the difference is the hiring channel. Student/new-grad gated by channel, not by explicit wording.

roles.title: Quantitative Researcher (Full-Time - Master's/Bachelor's)
roles.eligibility: University board (degree candidates / postdocs / faculty). Requires unofficial transcripts and GPA. New-grad channel - the candidate is past this stage; the experienced Quantitative Researcher req is the right door.
roles.requirements: Strong analytical background (maths, physics, CS, statistics, engineering) | Statistical expertise | Programming, C++ preferred | Data analysis and research framework experience | Interest in trading and financial markets (finance background not required)
roles.notes: Listed for completeness only. There is a parallel 'Quantitative Researcher (Full-Time - PhD+)' req at https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/radixuniversity/jobs/7841874002, also Chicago/New York/Amsterdam, which the candidate does not qualify for (no PhD).

roles.title: Quantitative Technologist (Full-Time - DevOps & Systems Engineering)
roles.eligibility: University board (new-grad channel). Did not open the full posting body; title and locations (Chicago / New York / Amsterdam) verified from the board listing.
roles.requirements: Not read in detail - infrastructure/DevOps and systems engineering flavoured Quantitative Technologist track; see the C++ Developer variant for the shared technologist criteria
roles.notes: Borderline for the C++ track - this is the infra/DevOps variant of the technologist role rather than a trading-systems C++ seat. Included because it is core infrastructure at a firm with only one in-scope office, but it is a weaker fit than the experienced Quantitative Technologist req.

existing_rows_audit.detail: The Chicago office is real (353 N Clark St Ste 1600, per https://radixtrading.co/), but 'Research Software Engineer' is not a title Radix uses on either of its two Greenhouse boards. The closest live Chicago reqs are 'Quantitative Technologist' (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/radixexperienced/jobs/6629869002) and 'HPC Systems Engineer' (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/radixexperienced/jobs/8121869002, Chicago/New York only). Chicago is also out of scope for this pass (US), and the row's '$300-400k' figure is not stated anywhere on the postings - both boards say only 'competitive salary plus quarterly bonus'.

notes: Radix Trading has exactly three offices - Chicago (HQ), New York, and Amsterdam (Strawinskylaan 1567) - confirmed on its own site at https://radixtrading.co/. Amsterdam is the only in-scope location; there is no London, Dublin, Singapore, Hong Kong, Shanghai or Tokyo presence. Amsterdam was reportedly chosen over London for post-Brexit regulatory reasons (secondary sourcing, not confirmed by the firm's site). The firm splits hiring across two Greenhouse boards linked from its homepage: radixexperienced (prior work experience) and radixuniversity (degree candidates, postdocs, faculty) - the candidate should use the experienced board. Every Amsterdam-tagged req is a multi-city listing shared with Chicago and New York, so the Amsterdam seat is not independently confirmed for any of them; the firm is only ~125 people total. No compensation figure is published on any posting, so all comp_local fields are empty - the existing sheet's $300-400k for Chicago should be treated as unsourced. No ML Performance or Trader roles are open in scope: the only ML/HPC-adjacent req, 'HPC Systems Engineer', is tagged Chicago and New York only, and Radix posts no trader titles at all (research and technologist are the two seat types). Out-of-scope Amsterdam reqs not listed: 'Quantitative Business Analyst' and 'Compliance Specialist - Amsterdam'.
